newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish finmin promises more jobs, cutting deficit.
newsitem.headline: Swedish finmin promises more jobs, cutting deficit.

text.p: Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said late on Monday that Sweden will meet its target to halve unemployment by the year 2000.
"We managed to straighten state finances out and I promise that we will also meet the unemployment target," Asbrink said at a public meeting in the southern Swedish town of Landskrona.
The issue needs to be given higher priority, he said.
"The task is not only confined to labour market policies. The entire economic policy must be directed towards the struggle for new jobs. That is why I feel so strongly for this issue," Asbrink said.
The important thing was to create new jobs even if this meant temporary jobs subsidised by the government, Asbrink said.
He said it was important to promote private enterprise and that doing so should be part of Social Democratic policies.
Asbrink said Sweden's 1996 budget deficit would be about three percent of gross domestic product (GDP), the level of fiscal balance sought by many candidates for the single European currency.
"After having been at the bottom of the class, Sweden now will start to take a top position," he said.
The government plans to cut the deficit to 2.6 percent of GDP this year and to have a balanced budget next year.
Thereafter, the budget should stay in surplus, giving Sweden the opportunity to pay off its debts, Asbrik said.
"Everything indicates we will reach those targets," he said.
